answer: Tie each agent to an outside credential through a zero-knowledge nullifier. The operator proves they hold one entry in a registry, say a licensed business list, and derives a nullifier unique to this network without revealing which entry. Reuse the same credential and the nullifier repeats, so the second sign-up is refused. A sybil farm can't forge new registry entries, so its pile of accounts shrinks from a canyon to a knoll: one seat per real credential.
